chapter: Blackbirds, Carmen Jones and the Ziegfeld Follies
title: Doubling uptown at the Lafayette and downtown at the Follies
summary: Going from the loud Lafayette to the silent Follies house, with cab-driver trouble, Bubbles tells Harry Leroy he keeps dancing to keep the applause up.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: the ridiculous to the sublime. When we left the Lafayette Theater to go downtown to the Ziegfeld Theater you could hear a pin fall downtown. Uptown, man, you couldn't hear your ears. You didn't know what was happening uptown. Downtown you darsn't spoil a song, it was so quiet, you know.
And we did that, I had to get Ruth Etting's husband to come up a couple of times to go down with us because we had some difficulties with the cab drivers. But we got that straight.
Running the car, I don't know whether he was jealous or what his story was, looked like a frame-up. I forget -- Gimp was his name. Gimp, that was Ruth Etting's husband.
But anyway we were coming downtown to do the show and we're downtown, I said to Harry Leroy, "How's it going, Harry?"

"Man, how do you do it?" "How do you do what," I says. He says, "How do you keep the audience still applauding for you like you did the opening night." I says, "I just have to keep on dancing, man, are you kidding." "You let up on yours, you got enough on opening night, huh? I didn't have enough." "I didn't get a good opening night. I had to follow everything on opening night, justlook what time I went on the stage?" I just gotta go keep on dancing and we were just as big after the opening as we were the opening. The audience was just as enthused and we were tearing that building down, man.
